newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Oerlikon sees higher 1996 net profit.
newsitem.headline: Oerlikon sees higher 1996 net profit.

text.p: Arms-to-fashion group Oerlikon-Buehrle Holding AG said 1996 net profit would be considerably higher than the 4.0 million Swiss francs the year before but below the 1994 level of 75.0 million.
Oerlikon said in a provisional statement on 1996 financial results that operating profit was substantially higher than the previous year's 139 million Swiss francs.
Sales were down 200 million at 3.6 billion Swiss francs.
Other than sales, Oerlikon did not provide exact figures.
It said the 1996 results would be published after a meeting of the board of directors scheduled in late March.
Referring to the individual divisions, Oerlikon said shoe and fashion maker Bally "held its previous year's sales".

Oerlikon said surface and vacuum technology unit Balzers and Leybold would have raised sales by around 90 million Swiss francs but showed a decrease due to the divestment of Pfeiffer as required by anti-trust authorities.
At military and space technology unit Oerlikon-Contraves, sales were down by around 100 million Swiss francs "as anticipated".

Small aircraft maker Pilaaturs and real state unit Immobilien "fell slightly short of their previous year's high level", Oerlikon said. "The group's net debt is now significantly below 1.2 billion Swiss francs," it said.
